kata.name: State-discovery near-floor control - a two-state machine where the frozen four-cell transition sample catches every injected fault
kata.series_report: docs/ref/ploeh-grounding.md §6 candidate 4 (reverse state-machine kata); fixtures/katas/state-discovery/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-lgl.4
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: at the two-state/two-event floor the conventional four-cell sample catches every injected fault; the probe buys zero unique detections (killed)

expected.detail: retarget On/stop: the sample asserts the documented target, so the conventional arm catches the executed eq2 violation on cell On/stop
drop Off/start's transition: the sample asserts the transition exists, so the conventional arm catches the executed dangling on cell Off/start

commands: python3 prototype/state_discovery_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: 5 entries, 3 unique elements; baseline sha256 pinned
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/state-discovery/near-floor.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/state-discovery/near-floor-fault-retarget.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/state-discovery/near-floor-fault-missing-exit.ct.json --json  # exit 4, 1 dangling

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/state_discovery_baseline.py --assert: a frozen four-cell sample (Off/start, Off/stop, On/start, On/stop) of transition-table assertions; catches both injected faults (2/2), zero unique detections for the probe.

baseline.artifact: prototype/state_discovery_baseline.py sha256:7d98b54bb65ea4e4c00962fc1d0e3e57ce19acb134f5d767b1177badd11fec3e (frozen transition-table sample; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: control scope: every injected fault lies inside the pre-registered four-cell sample
expressibility_gap.why: the near-floor control measures what a complete transition-table sample catches; it says nothing about faults outside the sample, which is the scoped claim of the positive entries

discrepancies: Control scope: the injected faults are behavior-changing and cell-local; a fault outside the sample is the positive band's claim, not a claim that this control is exhaustive.
procedure: 1. The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/state-discovery/ before any recorded run (README.md, faults.json); nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/state_discovery_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: frozen per-fixture samples of (state,event) cells asserting cell->transition, source/event/target agreement. Cells outside the sample are never inspected.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, plus `catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 1 --json` where the discovery questions belong to the entry; the construction probe is the same binary refusing an unparseable document.

4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements cell:<State>/<Event>; unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. Hypothesized underconstraint findings and executed construction rejections are recorded but never counted as detections.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
